A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PsyCoProfile/PsyCoTalk research. Main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A.1-A.8 are readable and matchable despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original diagnostic-accuracy results, psychiatrist evaluations, EMR distribution analyses and dialogue-diversity experiments, including English-generation results in Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports evaluation-sample composition and qualitative findings from early symptom-rating experiments.

M1.justification: The EMR and experience-generation pipeline, HDSM/DCT controller and three-agent architecture remain unchanged. Binary symptom ratings were already used in v1. Added explanations and expert-review details do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same four-disorder coverage, 502 EMRs, 3,000 Chinese dialogues, clinical and existing-corpus comparisons, and 205 English dialogues compared with AlexanderStreet. No dataset, language or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 newly reports a qualitative comparison between four-level symptom-rating agents and binary thresholding. The quantitative comparator sets in Section 5 and Appendix A.2, including the diagnostic-model baselines and comparison corpora, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The newly reported early comparison introduces a four-level symptom-rating condition alongside binary thresholding, although its detailed protocol is unspecified. Existing evaluation metrics, sample counts and generation settings remain unchanged; random selection of the existing 50 evaluated dialogues is newly disclosed.

E4.justification: v2 adds a brief qualitative failure analysis of four-level symptom ratings and a sample-versus-corpus composition check supporting clinician-evaluation representativeness. Existing intra-EMR diversity, cross-lingual analyses and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The McNemar test with p = 7 x 10^-6 and intra-EMR diversity reporting of 0.647 +/- 0.030 already appear in v1 and remain unchanged. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds sample/full-corpus proportions, including depression 0.35/0.38 and female 0.53/0.50, and reports inconsistent outputs and invalid transitions with four-level ratings. Existing results in Tables 1-6 and the diagnostic accuracies of 0.22 versus 0.31 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 1 and the diversity definitions in Appendix A.2 are unchanged. The added duration and impairment examples explain HDSM nodes already documented in Appendix A.5; they introduce no new formal definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about the clinically grounded pipeline, 502 EMRs, over 130 diagnostic states and 3,000 comorbidity dialogues. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of severity preservation, disorder selection and evaluation adequacy, acknowledges Reddit demographic/cultural skew, and specifies clinical-use restrictions. However, its new blanket statement that no real patient data are used conflicts with retained descriptions of real clinical comparison data.

D1.justification: v2 discloses iterative EMR review by eight psychiatrists, random sampling of the existing evaluation set and evaluator consent. It adds a repository pointer claiming code/data availability and explicitly requires a signed data-use agreement. These additions document review and access arrangements without establishing experimental reruns.

R1.justification: Six references are added: Mohammadkhani, Shankman and Brodey support discussion of clinical validation; Qi, Gabriel and Yang contextualize clinician-evaluation scale. The related-work section and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized expansions affect generation review, binary-rating rationale, evaluation, limitations and ethics. Acknowledgement and Reproducibility Statement sections are added. Most prose and the main section and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All six numbered tables and fourteen figures retain their content and designs. Reflow moves Table 5 before Appendix A.2.3, changes state-inventory table breaks, and separates Figure 8 from its explanatory text across pages 22-23 in v2.

improvement.justification: Added sampling details, methodological rationale, limitations and repository information improve documentation. However, new ethics assertions deny real patient-data use and restrict human involvement to five evaluators, conflicting with retained clinical-data comparisons and the newly disclosed eight-psychiatrist review. With the main empirical evidence unchanged, these competing gains and reporting inconsistencies prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
